notes: BDP system. Sister Payne shares styles 1-4 in shape, positions, era, and example serials. The page also lists Aquazone, BDP, Day and Night, and Weathermaster as related brands, but their serial systems were not verified in this batch and are not claimed as shared. Carrier is a related brand but its page states no serial system, so it is not claimed as sharing this system. Style 3 Canada reverses year/month positions vs US. Single-digit years in styles 3, 3-Canada, and 4 are encoded as digit-keyed letterTable maps because the schema digits kind does not support 1-character year slices; the mappings themselves are fully documented on the page. Schema-prose note: the locked schema says letterTable keys must be single uppercase letters; digit keys work in the builder (JSON keys are strings, table lookup is exact) but a future schema clarification (digitTable kind or prose update) should ratify this.

styles.era: 10-character format, week-year in first four digits
styles.notes: Week is 1st-2nd positions, year is 3rd-4th positions. Week decode for the example is 07.
Year is 1st-2nd positions, month is 3rd-4th positions.

Month letter is 1st position, M-Z skipping O and U for January-December. Year digit is 2nd position, 0-4 for 1980-1984. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.
Canadian variant only: year digit is 1st position, month letter is 2nd position, same tables as US style 3. Split from style 3 because one style cannot carry two position assignments.

Month letter is 1st position, A-L with no letters skipped. Year digit is 2nd position, 0-9 for 1970-1979. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.

Year letter begins with L for 1960 and cycles to H for 1979, skipping O, Q, and Z. Week is the 1st-2nd positions; the example week is 46. Split from the one-digit-week variant because fixed position ranges cannot express both.
Same year-letter table as style 5a. Week is the 1st position only; the example week is 2.
